Procurement reviewed Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and has two areas they want clearer language on before we route to legal: 1) the new frequency-based discount bands (Section 2.3) and whether those are applied retroactively or on the next billing period; 2) the interaction between the floor guarantee and monthly burst proration (we have seasonal spikes and need to understand true-up mechanics).

Attached is the redline from our side (Hollis_ef_redline.pdf) and a short worksheet showing hypothetical monthly usage. High level asks: can Redwood confirm whether discounts are credited back in the same invoice cycle, and if not, can you add explicit a) lookback period and b) proration formula so our finance team can model cost? Also, we asked to cap the stabilizer carry-forward at 20% of the monthly committed tokens — can Redwood accept that?

Appreciate a quick read — we are aiming to finalize order form language this week.

Elisabeth, thanks — this is helpful and the worksheet made the scenario very clear. Short answers up front: discounts are not retroactively credited to past invoices; they apply prospectively to the next invoice after the band is triggered. However, we can add a defined lookback/true-up window and an explicit proration formula so your FP&A can model it.

Proposed compromise we discussed internally:
- Lookback / true-up window: 30 days from the end of the month in which a band was triggered. We will calculate a one-time credit on the following invoice for the delta between invoiced amount and the amount that would have applied under the higher discount band for that period.
- Proration for seasonal spikes: when a monthly peak exceeds committed tokens by >50% we apply a pro-rated stabilized rate for the overage rather than the full floor; this prevents double-counting of both floor guarantees and spike credits.
- Stabilizer carry-forward cap: we can accept a cap, but propose 25% of monthly committed tokens rather than 20% to preserve coverage for anticipated bursts.

If that aligns, we will produce a clean redline with defined formulas (simple math description and an example row) and a companion spreadsheet with calculations.

I’ve looped in Laura (contracts) and Karthik (pricing) to confirm legal/finance acceptability — Laura, can we greenlight the 30-day true-up and 25% cap? Karthik — we’ll want the example numbers populated in the Pricing_Schedule_FrequencyBands.xlsx.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben — quick internal note. From a contracts standpoint: 30-day true-up is reasonable and keeps us operationally simple. The proration language needs to be explicit: we should include the formula and an example line item in the exhibit so it does not become an interpretation fight later. Draft language suggestion: "If monthly usage U exceeds committed tokens C in month M, any O = U - C that exceeds 50% of C will be billed at the overage rate R_overage prorated by (O / U) and eligible for a one-time true-up adjustment as defined below."

On the cap: finance prefers 25% but legal is comfortable pushing 22.5% if Hollis insists. My recommendation: propose 25% now, include a fallback acceptance of 22.5% in the negotiation notes. Karthik — please add the revenue impact for 20/22.5/25% to the spreadsheet.

Elisabeth — looping back with concrete language and an attached worked example. Key points in the redline (attached):
1) True-up window: 30 days (applies prospectively and gives you a single credit on the following invoice). Example row included for March usage.
2) Proration rule for spikes: overage units greater than 50% of committed tokens are eligible for prorated overage treatment (formula shown).
3) Stabilizer carry-forward cap: proposed 25% with optional fallback to 22.5% if Hollis requests.
4) Floor interaction: clarified that the floor guarantee establishes a minimum monthly payment but does not prevent credits from true-ups; credits reduce the following invoice but do not retroactively reduce prior payments.

If you can confirm the 25% carry-forward is a hard stop for you, we will finalize the redline and circulate to legal for signature routing. Attaching the redline and the Pricing_Schedule_FrequencyBands.xlsx with the three sensitivity runs (20/22.5/25%).
